conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Locale specification (how user and system defaults defined; at least one user and one system default)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §8.2.1 (cite.py OK 'The implementor shall specify the manner in which the user default locale is defined'; OK 'The capability of setting the system default locale from COBOL is not provided'). A.1-118 need not be documented: VOLUNTARY row. Verified by code (LocaleState ctor lines 185-187: Determine(COBOL_USER_LOCALE, CurrentCulture) / Determine(COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE, InstalledUICulture), catch -> '' root; SystemDefault get-only; RunUnit.Locale = new()) and probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s4/probe/p118.cob (--std 2023, run via dotnet p118.dll): de-DE/fr-FR env -> USR 24.09.2026 / SYS 24/09/2026; COBOL_USER_LOCALE=ja-JP -> USR 2026/09/24; DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1 -> both 09/24/2026, rc 0; LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 -> both 24/09/2026 (the culture fallback). No spec-derived test pins the environment-variable or culture fallback arms (LocaleStateTests pin the §14.6.6 state mechanics, not the defaults' source), hence Pinned by —.
rows.rule-text: Locale specification (how user and system defaults defined; at least one user and one system default). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation. The implementor may specify that the user locale and the system locale are the same locale. (8.2, Locales)

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.24.3 "File-name-1 shall be described in a sort-merge file description entry in the data division" -> OK §14.9.24.3 2). BindMerge resolves the name through ctx.Validation.ResolveFile (undeclared -> §8.4.2.1 report) and refuses `!file.IsSortMerge` with COBOLNET1757 'MERGE file ... is not described in a sort-merge description entry'. Probe mfd (`MERGE F3 ... ` with F3 under an FD) -> rc=70 COBOLNET1757. A legal SD operand compiles and runs (mbase, mrt4e). No MERGE-specific spec-derived negative golden located -> test-ref empty. || editions as adjudicated: 85/2002/2014/2023 (clause text)
rows.rule-text: File-name-1 shall be described in a sort-merge file description entry in the data division.

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.24.3 "Alphabet-name-1 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric collating sequence" -> OK §14.9.24.3 5). SortBindCollating looks alphabet-name-1 up in ctx.Data.Alphabets only; a FOR NATIONAL alphabet there -> COBOLNET0898 (probe msr5 `FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS NN`), an undeclared name -> COBOLNET0898. Every alphanumeric alphabet form references a collating sequence (§12.3.7 Table 6: UTF-8/UTF-16 are the only CCS-only operands and UTF-8 is confined to the FOR NATIONAL branch — probe msr5u8 rejected at the ALPHABET clause), so no further case exists. Cosmetic: the diagnostic cites §14.9.40.3 SR2 (SORT's rule) for MERGE. || editions as adjudicated: 85/2002/2014/2023 (clause text; the FOR ALPHANUMERIC spelling is 2002+)
rows.rule-text: Alphabet-name-1 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric collating sequence.

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.24.3 "Alphabet-name-2 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national collating sequence" -> OK §14.9.24.3 6). Alphabet-name-2 is looked up in ctx.Data.NationalAlphabets and its HasCollatingSequence is checked: an alphanumeric alphabet in the second position (msr6 `IS AA AA`) or FOR NATIONAL (msr6b) -> COBOLNET0898; a UTF-16 national alphabet (CCS only, Table 6) -> COBOLNET0898 (msr6u16); a NATIVE national alphabet accepted (mcoll2/3 at 2002/2023). || editions as adjudicated: 2002/2014/2023 (alphabet-name-2 / FOR NATIONAL is the national class; below 2002 the form is refused by COBOLNET0872, probe mcoll2/mcoll3 --std 85)
rows.rule-text: Alphabet-name-2 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national collating sequence.

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.24.3 "The words THROUGH and THRU are equivalent" -> OK §14.9.24.3 8). Both spellings parse to the same output-procedure phrase and SortRange composes procedure-name-1 THRU procedure-name-2 identically: probes mthru and mthrough (OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS OP1 THRU/THROUGH OP2) both compile rc=0. || editions as adjudicated: 85/2002/2014/2023 (clause text)
rows.rule-text: The words THROUGH and THRU are equivalent.

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: data-names after KEY in decreasing significance regardless of KEY-phrase division; a) ASCENDING low->high, b) DESCENDING high->low, per relation-condition comparison; 'The words ASCENDING and DESCENDING are transitive across all occurrences of data-name-1 until another occurrence of the word ASCENDING or DESCENDING is encountered.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 3) and 3) b)). Code: grammar mergeKeyPhrase = ON? (ASCENDING|DESCENDING) KEY? dataReferenceList, so the direction word governs every data-name of its list (transitivity); BindMerge appends keys phrase by phrase in statement order (significance); KeyColumns.Compare walks keys most-significant first and negates for Descending; comparison per class (numeric algebraic, alphanumeric/national under the GR5 sequence) = relation-condition rules (GR5 itself is part 1 / PB678 landed). Probe probe/merge-p2/m1.cob `ON ASCENDING KEY M-A DESCENDING KEY M-B M-C` (M-B PIC 9, M-C PIC X): output A9Z*, A9Y, A5Q, A1Z, B5A* - M-A ascending, M-B descending, M-C descending by transitivity - identical at --std 85 and 2023. No spec-derived golden exercises a multi-key/DESCENDING MERGE (SortMergeDifferentialTests.Merge_EqualKeys_KeepUsingFileOrder is a legacy differential and does not qualify).
rows.rule-text: The data-names following the word KEY are listed from left to right in the MERGE statement in order of decreasing significance without regard to how they are divided into KEY phrases. The leftmost data-name is the major key, the next data-name is the next most significant key, etc. a) When the ASCENDING phrase is specified, the merged sequence is from the lowest value of the contents of the data items identified by the key data-names to the highest value, according to the rules for comparison of operands in a relation condition. b) When the DESCENDING phrase is specified, the merged sequence is from the highest value of the contents of the data items identified by the key data-names to the lowest value, according to the rules for comparison of operands in a relation condition. The words ASCENDING and DESCENDING are transitive across all occurrences of data-name-1 until another occurrence of the word ASCENDING or DESCENDING is encountered.

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: equal-key records return a) 'Follows the order of the associated input files as specified in the MERGE statement.' b) 'Is such that all records associated with one input file are returned prior to the return of records from another input file.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 4) b)). Code: NextInput marks each USING stream's start in statement order; Merge picks the head with STRICT less-than, so an equal head never displaces an earlier stream, and within a stream records keep file order; a stream's equal-key run is fully drained before a later stream's equal record because the earlier stream's next equal head again wins the tie. Probe probe/merge-p2/m1.cob: key A9Z in F1(1 rec), F2(2 recs), F3(1 rec) -> A9ZF1-1, A9ZF2-1, A9ZF2-2, A9ZF3-1; key B5A F1 before F3 - both halves. Only covering test is the legacy differential SortMergeDifferentialTests.Merge_EqualKeys_KeepUsingFileOrder (AssertSameAsLegacy) - does not qualify; test-needed.
rows.rule-text: When, according to the rules for the comparison of operands in a relation condition, the contents of all the key data items of one record are equal to the contents of the corresponding key data items of one or more other records, the order of return of these records: a) Follows the order of the associated input files as specified in the MERGE statement. b) Is such that all records associated with one input file are returned prior to the return of records from another input file.

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'During the execution of the output procedure, no statement may be executed manipulating the file referenced by or accessing the record area associated with file-name-2 or file-name-3.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 10)). This is a constraint on the PROGRAM with no exception condition and no prescribed consequence, so it asks nothing of the implementation beyond not depending on such access; the rule names no diagnostic and the range is dynamic, so a compile-time refusal would reject legal source whose violating path never executes. Code: EmitMerge completes every USING transfer (implicit OPEN/READ/CLOSE) and the k-way merge BEFORE entering the output procedure, so a violating statement meets a closed connector (deterministic, within 'undefined'); nothing in the implementation relies on file-name-2/-3 being untouched during the procedure. No finding. (The early CLOSE is GR7 c)'s timing question - part 1, not this rule.)
rows.rule-text: During the execution of the output procedure, no statement may be executed manipulating the file referenced by or accessing the record area associated with file-name-2 or file-name-3.

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'During the execution of any USE procedure implicitly invoked while executing the MERGE statement, no statement may be executed manipulating the file referenced by or accessing the record area associated with file-name-2, file-name-3, or file-name-4.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 11)). A constraint on the program with no exception condition and no prescribed consequence - nothing for the implementation to enforce or detect (GR12's closing paragraph restates it for file-name-4 with 'shall not'). Code: the as-if statements' USE procedures are invoked via EmitTransferUse (seqIo.EmitUseHook); the transfer's own state (READ/WRITE loops, CobolSort store) does not depend on the USE procedure leaving the connectors alone beyond the loop's own unsuccessful-status exit, so a violating program gets deterministic results within 'undefined'. No finding. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 in substance (USE procedures invoked from the implicit transfers belong to the 2002 exception model)
rows.rule-text: During the execution of any USE procedure implicitly invoked while executing the MERGE statement, no statement may be executed manipulating the file referenced by or accessing the record area associated with file-name-2, file-name-3, or file-name-4.

rows.subject: MERGE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'Additional rules affecting the execution of the MERGE statement are given in 12.4.5, File control entry, General rules 3 and 4.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 14)); target: 'The association occurs at the time of execution of an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement that referenced file-name-1' ... 'If the association cannot be made ... the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement is unsuccessful.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 -> OK §12.4.5.3 3)). GR4 is implementor-defined content (DOC-A.1-73 / DOC-A.1-10; GR-12.4.5.3-4 adjudicated CONFORMS in the file-control-entry batch). Code: every MERGE implicit OPEN goes through EmitImplicitOpen with seqIo.ExecutingElementArgs(file) - the executing element's ASSIGN spec (kb/Work PB673) - so association happens at MERGE execution. Probe probe/merge-p2/m6.cob (USING I1 `ASSIGN USING N1`, I2, GIVING `ASSIGN USING NG`): M1 with N1='mp2aA.dat' -> AAA,CCC into mp2aO1.dat; M2 with N1='mp2aB.dat' -> BBB,CCC into mp2aO2.dat (re-association per MERGE execution); M3 with N1=SPACES -> S1='31', MERGE terminated (I2 untouched, mp2aO3.dat never created) = 'the MERGE statement is unsuccessful'. The SD's own ASSIGN is never associated because the store is in memory - unobservable. No existing golden runs MERGE over ASSIGN USING (pb324/pb673 contain no SORT/MERGE statement) - test-needed. || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the cross-reference; 12.4.5.3 GR3 b)/GR4's USING phrase follows that phrase's own edition, owned by open PB746/PB674 per the file-control-entry adjudication)
rows.rule-text: Additional rules affecting the execution of the MERGE statement are given in 12.4.5, File control entry, General rules 3 and 4.
